newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: GTE executive, 4 others die in Guatemala air crash.
newsitem.headline: GTE executive, 4 others die in Guatemala air crash.

text.p: Five people including Bruce Haddad, the senior vice president of international operations for GTE Corp and his wife, died on Wednesday in a plane crash near Guatemala City, aviation officials said.
The plane had taken off from Caracas, Venezuela, picked up the Haddads in Lima, Peru, and was to make a stop in Guatemala City on its way to Dallas, Texas when it crashed.
"I called Peru to confirm the list of passengers, who were Bruce Haddad and Mrs. Dorothy Haddad," Ronald Peter Zineri, Guatemala's director of civil aviation, told Reuters.
Zineri said that three Venezuelan crew members, identified as pilot Carlos Izquierdo, Francisco Nieto and Rafael Ramon, also died.
The corporate jet, a Westwind 24 chartered from the Venezuelan company Inversiones Liftoff, slammed into the side of a mountain about 3:30 a.m. local (0930 GMT) Zineri said.
"The airplane is completely destroyed and there are no survivors," Rony Paz, civil aviation chief of operations, told Reuters.
Zineri said the plane hit a small mountain near the Pacaya Volcano about 15 miles (25 km) from the capital. He said the weather was good and visibility clear.
"The tower told the pilot, and it's on tape, a few seconds before the accident that he was off course," Zineri said.

Witnesses at the crash site said the airplane went down in a steep, wooded part of the mountain and pieces of the airplane were scattered over a wide area. "It's pretty ugly. There were shoes all over the place and some clothes hanging in the trees," Reuters photographer Rutilio Enamourado said.
U.S. Consul Duke Lokka visited the scene of the accident and told reporters the U.S. Embassy in Guatemala would be in touch with family members regarding disposition of the bodies.

The last fatal airplane crash in Guatemala, not including two-seaters, was Nov. 2 when 14 people died as a small tourist aircraft crashed in an ecological reserve near the world famous Mayan ruins of Tikal.
